Leave-One-Out Sensitivity Analysis

Source: R/loo.R
loo.Rd

Refits the model dropping one observation (or one country/group) at a time. Returns the impact on coefficient estimates, fitted values, and \(\xi\) (total population size estimate).

Usage

loo(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'uncounted'
loo(object, by = c("obs", "country"), verbose = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

An "uncounted" object (fitted model).

...

Additional arguments (ignored).

by

What to leave out: "obs" drops one row at a time, "country" drops all rows for one country at a time (requires countries to have been specified in the original fit).

verbose

Logical; print progress?

Value

An object of class "uncounted_loo" with components:

coefficients

Matrix (n_drops x p): coefficients from each refit.

xi

Data frame with \(\xi\) estimates from each refit.

dropped

Character vector: label of dropped observation or country.

dfbeta

Matrix (n_drops x p): influence on the coefficients, \(\hat{\beta} - \hat{\beta}_{(-i)}\), the same sign as stats::dfbeta(). Positive means the unit pulls the coefficient up.

dxi

Numeric vector: influence on the population size for a fixed target, using the refit's coefficients on all rows (see Details).

dxi_subset

Numeric vector: change in population size when the unit also leaves the target (see Details).

full_coefs

Full-model coefficients.

full_ps

Full-model population size data frame.

full_ps_total

Full-model total \(\hat{\xi}\).

by

The by argument used.

converged

Logical vector: whether each refit converged.

n_drops

Number of leave-one-out iterations.

Details

Purpose. LOO sensitivity analysis assesses how much each observation (or country) influences the estimated population size. An observation with a large \(|\Delta\xi|\) relative to the full-model \(\hat{\xi}\) is "influential" and may warrant closer inspection.

by = "obs" vs by = "country". With by = "obs", each row is dropped individually (n refits). This identifies individual data points that drive the estimate, useful for detecting outliers or data errors. With by = "country", all rows belonging to one country are dropped simultaneously (one refit per country). This measures each country's overall contribution to \(\hat{\xi}\) and is more relevant for assessing structural sensitivity: would the conclusion change if a country were excluded?

Interpretation of dxi. dxi measures influence on the estimate for a fixed target population: \(\Delta\xi_i = \sum_j N_j^{\hat\alpha_{j(-i)}} - \sum_j N_j^{\hat\alpha_j}\), where both sums run over all rows and \(\hat\alpha_{(-i)}\) comes from the refit without unit \(i\). It therefore reflects only how the coefficients move.

  • \(\Delta\xi_i < 0\): without \(i\) the estimate is lower (the unit was pulling the estimate up).

  • \(\Delta\xi_i > 0\): without \(i\) the estimate is higher (the unit was pulling the estimate down).

dxi_subset is the change when the unit also leaves the target: the total of popsize() on the refit, over the remaining rows only, minus \(\hat\xi\). It is mostly negative because it includes the unit's own share of \(\hat\xi\), so it is not an influence measure, but it answers “what would we estimate if this unit were not in the data at all?”

Examples

# Simulate synthetic data
set.seed(42)
n_obs <- 15
sim_data <- data.frame(
  country = rep(paste0("C", 1:5), each = 3),
  year    = rep(2018:2020, 5),
  N       = rpois(n_obs, lambda = 500000),
  n       = rpois(n_obs, lambda = 1000),
  m       = rpois(n_obs, lambda = 50)
)

fit <- estimate_hidden_pop(
  data = sim_data, observed = ~m, auxiliary = ~n,
  reference_pop = ~N, method = "poisson",
  countries = ~country
)
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.046). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Estimated gamma is at its lower bound (1e-10); the optimum may lie outside gamma_bounds = c(1e-10, 0.5).

# LOO by observation (drops one row at a time)
loo_obs <- loo(fit, by = "obs")
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.064). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.211). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.057). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.025). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.451). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.051). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.087). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.064). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
print(loo_obs)       # top 10 most influential observations
#> Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis
#> Dropped by: obs 
#> N iterations: 15 
#> Converged: 15 / 15 
#> 
#> Full model xi: 8.2 
#> LOO xi range: 0 to 49.6 
#> 
#> Most influential (by |delta xi|):
#>  dropped  dxi pct_change
#>       13 41.4     503.14
#>       12 29.6     360.64
#>        6 12.9     157.44
#>        9  9.6     116.51
#>        4  8.4     102.78
#>        1  8.2      99.69
#>        8 -8.2     -99.51
#>        3 -7.3     -88.56
#>       14  7.0      84.99
#>       11 -3.4     -41.85
summary(loo_obs)     # coefficient and xi stability
#> Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis
#> Dropped by: obs 
#> N iterations: 15 (converged: 15 )
#> 
#> === Coefficient stability ===
#>            full  loo_mean   loo_sd   loo_min   loo_max
#> alpha -0.045833 -0.052940 0.131550 -0.450711  0.091103
#> beta  -0.726555 -0.741571 0.278221 -1.583679 -0.435062
#> 
#> === Xi stability ===
#> Full xi: 8.2 
#> LOO mean: 14.6 
#> LOO range: 0 to 49.6 
#> Max |%change|: 503.14 %
plot(loo_obs)        # bar plot of dxi

plot(loo_obs, type = "coef")  # DFBETA plots per coefficient


# LOO by country (drops all rows for one country)
loo_ctry <- loo(fit, by = "country")
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.171). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
#> Warning: Some alpha values < 0 (min = -0.406). Consider using constrained = TRUE.
print(loo_ctry)

#> N iterations: 5 
#> Converged: 5 / 5
